DIRECTION B

Graphite Command Frame

Dark equipment casing wraps a warm cream work canvas. The shell reads as a machined enclosure; the canvas reads as paper inside it. Cyan-teal is the single signal colour — bright enough to register against the dark chrome, calm enough to sit beside ink on paper.

What stays grey · what becomes chrome · ink · colour

Chrome. TitleBar, ModeRail, Status Bar, and Context Sidebar are all in the dark casing system (#181B22 / #0F1118). They form a continuous matte envelope around the canvas; subtle inset highlight + deeper shadow give every chrome edge a fascia-plate feel.

Ink. Off-warm ink #E8E3D6 on chrome — warm enough to pair with the cream canvas. Black ink #1A1D24 on the canvas. Mono is reserved for hostnames, IPs, numerics.

Colour. Cyan-teal #2DBDBE is the single action colour: rollout buttons, active mode glow, focus ring, Cortex highlight. Status colours adjust their saturation for legibility on dark — partial-amber stays bright; deferred drops to a cooler grey. Domain accent bars are bright enough to read on dark.

Implementation risks

Dark sidebar contrast. Dark sidebar pushes ink-on-chrome contrast hard. The 12 px row text needs minimum #E8E3D6 on #181B22 — verify with the FRA-CORE site list (long, dense). If it fails AA at 12 px, bump the type to 12.5 px on dark rows.
Cream canvas off-white. A warm canvas is a real commitment — every chart well, every captured screenshot, and every Babylon viewport must be tuned to look right on cream, not on pure white. Topology Babylon scene already assumes white background; budget a re-tune.
Existing components. Every component currently styled "white panel on light app" must be re-tuned. The lift is larger than direction A or C. If we ship this, plan a single sweep stage before any other product work resumes.
Tenant skinning. Bright domain accents are saturated. If a tenant ever asks for a custom brand colour close to one of them (a foundation-cobalt brand would collide with the Foundation strip), we will have a conflict. Reserve domain hues as system tokens.

Surface treatments

  • TitleBar. Full dark fascia. Brand mark + domain pill on the left; cream-tinted ink. Env selector and Cortex input are subtly recessed (rgba-white overlays). Window controls flush right, close on critical-red on hover.
  • ModeRail. Deeper dark (#0F1118) — the rail reads as recessed below the titlebar. Group headers carry the domain orientation strip; on dark the bright domain hues (#5887FF / #FFA64D / #FF6F8F / #B58CFF) become genuine identity anchors. Active row gets a cyan-teal inset glow and a tinted background.
  • Context Sidebar. Stays dark — part of the casing. White-on-dark rows; cyan-teal underlines the active row. This is the boldest divergence from direction A: a dark sidebar means the cream canvas comes out punchier, and the eye can't mistake nav for content.
  • Cortex overlay. A dark module floating above the cream canvas — chrome envelopes the same dark surface. Scope chips and matched-substring highlights are cyan-teal. The scrim is deeper than in A because the canvas underneath is bright cream.
  • Dashboard cards. Cream panel + 4 px left strip in the card's domain colour. Domain dot + label at top-left; state chip top-right. Card shadow is paired with an inset white highlight so panels lift slightly off the cream canvas without looking webby.

State semantics

Capability states are tuned brighter than direction A — they must survive on the dark casing for rail/sidebar LEDs. On the cream canvas the same hex registers fine; we use one set of values, not two. Critical is the only saturated red; blocked is softer.

Domain accents

Foundation cobalt-light · Run amber-light · Governance rose · Workshop violet-light. Tuned so each is clearly distinguishable on the dark rail. Together they make the rail genuinely navigable by colour — you can find Run mode at a glance because of the amber band.
